name: openssl
one_line: A crypto toolbox: hashes, encoding, symmetric encryption, certificates and keys, from one command.
plain: A crypto toolbox: hashes, encoding, symmetric encryption, certificates and keys, from one command.
The sections below show when to use it, real examples, and the options explained in plain English.
when: Hash a string or file; compare with a checksum.
Encode/decode base64; try AES with a known key.
Check RSA keys in a challenge.

examples.title: Hash a string (and avoid the newline trap)
examples.cmd: echo -n hello | openssl dgst -sha256; echo hello | openssl dgst -sha256

examples.title: Base64 both ways
examples.cmd: printf 'hello world' | openssl base64; echo ---; cat data.b64 | openssl base64 -d; echo

examples.title: Encrypt with a password and look at the file
examples.cmd: printf 'secret message' | openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -k letmein -out enc.bin; head -c 16 enc.bin | xxd; openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -k letmein -in enc.bin; echo
examples.output:
00000000: 5361 6c74 6564 5f5f edc6 a962 f609 a994  Salted__...b....
secret message

examples.title: Read a certificate
examples.cmd: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout k.pem -out c.pem -subj '/CN=demo.local/O=Lab' -days 1 2>/dev/null; openssl x509 -in c.pem -noout -subject -issuer
examples.output:
subject=CN = demo.local, O = Lab
issuer=CN = demo.local, O = Lab

mistakes: `-pbkdf2` and `-md sha256` differ across OpenSSL versions: decrypting old files may need the original options.
`openssl enc` is for study: never design real encryption with raw `enc`.
CSR vs certificate vs key are different PEM types: check the header line (`-----BEGIN ...`).
try: Encrypt a 48-byte message of repeating blocks with ECB and with CBC and compare the dumps.
Hash the contents of `hello.c` and verify with `sha256sum`.
Create a certificate with a different CN and read it back.
